flagship_directive: Determine matching upper and legal lower bounds for K_n(d;B,c) throughout d=o(n^{2/3}), thereby converting the asymptotic frontier into a sharp finite-error calibration rule.
critique: The note proves the advertised worst-case degree frontier: the martingale bound establishes sufficiency at d_n=o(n^{2/3}), while the repeated-star construction supplies a legal non-Gaussian boundary limit establishing necessity. It also proves ratio consistency only for the conservative spectral variance bound, not the exact randomization variance, and consequently establishes conservative rather than exact Wald coverage. The headline is faithful, but annotations repeatedly call proved lemmas and theorems “candidate,” “conjectured,” or contingent on independent verification, contradicting the completed proof text and impairing claim clarity. The exact order of K_n(d;B,c) within the normal regime remains open because the displayed one-fifth-power upper bound has no matching legal lower arrays. The narrow restriction to the fixed r=2 estimator and Perron ordering, together with the absence of finite-sample calibration on practically relevant graphs, limits the projected leading-journal score.
